story.summary: Create tests to use Home screen icons
story.description: With Org users, login to eCore and click on each of the Icons on the Home page, verify that you are taken to the correct page, and click Command Center in the upper left corner to return to the Home Page.

requirements.description: The journey is performed as an authenticated organization user of eCore Command Center.
requirements.originalText: With Org users, login to eCore

requirements.description: Every icon presented on the Home page can be activated by the user.
requirements.originalText: click on each of the Icons on the Home page

requirements.description: Activating a Home page icon takes the user to the page that icon stands for.
requirements.originalText: verify that you are taken to the correct page

requirements.description: A Command Center control in the upper left corner returns the user from a destination page to the Home page.
requirements.originalText: click Command Center in the upper left corner to return to the Home Page

acceptanceCriteria.description: An organization user who signs in successfully arrives at the eCore Command Center Home page.
acceptanceCriteria.originalText: With Org users, login to eCore
acceptanceCriteria.given: an organization user with correct organization sign-in details
acceptanceCriteria.when: they sign in to eCore Command Center
acceptanceCriteria.then: the eCore Command Center Home page is displayed to them

acceptanceCriteria.description: The Home page presents three activatable icons: New Transaction, Workspace and Preferences.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an organization user is on the eCore Command Center Home page
acceptanceCriteria.when: they look at the icons offered on the Home page
acceptanceCriteria.then: three icons are offered, named New Transaction, Workspace and Preferences, and each one can be activated
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: The story says 'each of the Icons' but never enumerates them, so the set cannot be taken from Jira. It was observed against the real QA application on 2026-09-01 and recorded in reports/validation/ETA-411-home-icons-probe.json: exactly three dashboard icons are rendered, each an anchor wrapping a dashboard_*.png image inside the #icon-buttons container, and each matching a heading of the same name. The set is evidence, not a business rule, and AMB-ETA-411-001 asks whether the story means these three tiles only.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Activating the New Transaction icon takes the user to the New Transaction page.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an organization user is on the eCore Command Center Home page
acceptanceCriteria.when: they activate the New Transaction icon
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are taken to the New Transaction page
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: The story requires that each icon leads to 'the correct page' but never says which page is correct for which icon. The destination was observed by navigation, not inferred from markup: activating this icon landed on /ssweb/setup/container/ct/newPackage.eo and the destination presented a 'Create Transaction' heading. See reports/validation/ETA-411-home-icons-probe.json navigationWalk. AMB-ETA-411-002 is resolved: the reviewer accepts the landing URL as proof that the correct page was reached. This destination also has a unique 'Create Transaction' heading available as a secondary check.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Activating the Workspace icon takes the user to the Workspace page.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an organization user is on the eCore Command Center Home page
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are taken to the Workspace page
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: As for AC-ETA-411-003, the destination is observed rather than stated in Jira: activating this icon landed on /ssweb/setup/workspace/workspace.eo. The destination exposed no heading unique to it, so the landing URL is the only observed discriminator. AMB-ETA-411-002 is resolved: the reviewer accepts the landing URL as proof. The residual risk is recorded in that resolution and is knowingly accepted.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Activating the Preferences icon takes the user to the Preferences page.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an organization user is on the eCore Command Center Home page
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are taken to the Preferences page
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: As for AC-ETA-411-003, the destination is observed rather than stated in Jira: activating this icon landed on /ssweb/setup/prefs/preferences.eo. The destination exposed no heading unique to it, so the landing URL is the only observed discriminator. AMB-ETA-411-002 is resolved: the reviewer accepts the landing URL as proof. The residual risk is recorded in that resolution and is knowingly accepted.

acceptanceCriteria.description: From the page reached by any Home page icon, activating the Command Center control in the upper left corner returns the user to the Home page.
acceptanceCriteria.originalText: click Command Center in the upper left corner to return to the Home Page
acceptanceCriteria.given: an organization user has reached a destination page by activating a Home page icon
acceptanceCriteria.when: they activate the Command Center control in the upper left corner
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are returned to the eCore Command Center Home page

acceptanceCriteria.description: The header navigation bar offers New Transaction and Workspace links that duplicate the Home page dashboard tiles of the same name.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an organization user is on the eCore Command Center Home page
acceptanceCriteria.when: they look at the header navigation bar
acceptanceCriteria.then: links named New Transaction and Workspace are offered, in addition to the dashboard tiles of the same name
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: AMB-ETA-411-001 was resolved by the reviewer as 'the dashboard tiles plus the header navigation duplicates'. That answer assumed the header duplicates all three tiles. It does not. The observed header exposes only a#header.new_transaction and a#header.workspace, alongside a#header.home and a#header.logout; there is no header Preferences link. Preferences is reachable from a menu link labelled 'Organization' instead, which is a different name for the same destination and is raised separately as AMB-ETA-411-006. This criterion therefore covers the two duplicates that were actually observed and does not assert a third that does not exist. Evidence: reports/validation/ETA-411-home-icons-probe.json topLeftControls.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Activating the New Transaction link in the header navigation bar takes the user to the New Transaction page.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an organization user is on the eCore Command Center Home page
acceptanceCriteria.when: they activate the New Transaction link in the header navigation bar
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are taken to the New Transaction page
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: In scope because AMB-ETA-411-001 was resolved to include the header navigation duplicates. The destination is taken from the link's href, /ssweb/setup/container/ct/newPackage.eo, which matches the dashboard tile destination confirmed by navigation. This header link was never activated during reconnaissance, so unlike AC-ETA-411-003 the destination is inferred from markup rather than observed. An href is not proof of navigation, because a redirect, an interstitial or a permission check can intervene. Confirming it is the first task of PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Activating the Workspace link in the header navigation bar takes the user to the Workspace page.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an organization user is on the eCore Command Center Home page
acceptanceCriteria.when: they activate the Workspace link in the header navigation bar
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are taken to the Workspace page
acceptanceCriteria.rationale: In scope because AMB-ETA-411-001 was resolved to include the header navigation duplicates. The destination is taken from the link's href, /ssweb/setup/workspace/workspace.eo, which matches the dashboard tile destination confirmed by navigation. As for AC-ETA-411-008, this header link was never activated during reconnaissance, so the destination is inferred from markup rather than observed and must be confirmed during PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION.

ambiguities.question: What exactly counts as an 'Icon on the Home page'? The Home page renders three dashboard tiles (New Transaction, Workspace, Preferences), but the header navigation bar repeats those same three names as text links, and a further menu exposes many more destinations including Configuration Changes, eAsset Analytics, Event Analytics, Infographics, Manage Scheduled Reports, Open Requests, Permission Analysis, Transaction Retention Analysis, User Activity Analysis, Vault Content, Organization, Vault, Tutorials, Support and About. Does ETA-411 mean the three dashboard tiles only, or a wider set?
ambiguities.impact: AC-ETA-411-002 currently scopes the story to the three dashboard tiles on the strength of the word 'Icons' and the dashboard_*.png imagery. If the wider navigation is in scope, this artifact is materially incomplete: roughly fifteen further destinations would each need their own criterion, and the capability boundary for home-navigation would be wrong.
ambiguities.resolution: Scope is the three Home page dashboard tiles plus the header navigation links that duplicate them. The wider menu of roughly fifteen further destinations is out of scope for ETA-411. Correction of record: the reviewer's answer said 'the three header nav duplicates', but only two exist. The observed header exposes a#header.new_transaction and a#header.workspace only; there is no header Preferences link. AC-ETA-411-007, AC-ETA-411-008 and AC-ETA-411-009 therefore cover two duplicates rather than three, and the question of whether the menu link labelled 'Organization' counts as a third route to Preferences is carried forward as AMB-ETA-411-006.

ambiguities.question: What evidence establishes that the user was 'taken to the correct page'? Every page in the application returns the identical browser title 'eOriginal Command Center', and the Workspace and Preferences destinations expose no heading unique to them - the only heading observed on them is a shared, hidden 'The attached documents must be in one of the following formats:' block that also appears elsewhere. The landing URL is currently the only reliable discriminator observed. Is asserting on the URL acceptable, or must each destination be identified by a named on-screen element?
ambiguities.impact: AC-ETA-411-003, AC-ETA-411-004 and AC-ETA-411-005 say 'taken to the New Transaction / Workspace / Preferences page' without fixing how that is proven. If URL assertions are unacceptable, a per-destination visible element must be named by a human before these criteria can be automated, because choosing one would be inventing an expectation the story does not state.
ambiguities.resolution: Asserting on the landing URL is acceptable proof that the user was taken to the correct page. No per-destination visible element needs to be named. The reviewer accepted this in preference to running a further page-signature probe. Residual risk, knowingly accepted and recorded here so it is not discovered later as a surprise: a URL assertion cannot distinguish a correctly rendered page from a page that reached the right address but rendered an error, an empty result or a permission refusal. Such a case would pass. If that risk later matters, the fix is to name a visible element per destination, which reopens this question rather than being a change of test detail.

ambiguities.question: Is the Home page icon set identical for every organization user, or does it vary by role, permission or organization configuration? The observation behind AC-ETA-411-002 was made with a single account.
ambiguities.impact: If the icon set is permission-dependent, AC-ETA-411-002 is only true for the observed account and the tests will be account-specific rather than a statement about the product. Further criteria and further test accounts would be needed. This overlaps AMB-ETA-351-006, which already flagged permission-limited Home page behaviour as unresolved; the two should be answered together rather than separately.
ambiguities.resolution: The reviewer states that the Home page icon set is identical for every organization user and does not vary by role, permission or organization configuration. This is recorded as the reviewer's assertion about intended product behaviour, not as an observation: reconnaissance used a single account, so the artifact holds no evidence either way. On that basis AC-ETA-411-002 is a statement about the product rather than about the observed account, and no second test account is required for ETA-411. AMB-ETA-351-006 raised the same question for ETA-351 and remains open there; this resolution does not close it.

ambiguities.question: Which release does ETA-411 belong to? The Jira issue carries no fixVersions value, yet this workflow instance was created as WF-ETA-411-R1.0 on a verbal instruction given in chat rather than on anything recorded in Jira.
ambiguities.impact: The release key propagates into the RTM partition, the coverage matrix and every @release- tag on every generated scenario. If 1.0 is wrong, all of that traceability is filed under the wrong release and a later correction means reissuing the artifacts rather than editing them.
ambiguities.resolution: Release 1.0 is confirmed by the reviewer. The Jira issue still carries no fixVersions value, so this artifact remains the only record of the release assignment. If Jira is later populated with a different release, the RTM partition, the coverage matrix and every @release- tag for this story are filed under the wrong release and must be reissued rather than edited.

ambiguities.question: The Command Center control in the upper left corner is not a link or a button. It is a plain div, id 'bannerBackground', class 'clickable', 216x45 pixels at the top left, carrying command_center.png as a CSS background image and a pointer cursor. It exposes no text, no alt text, no title and no accessible name, so assistive technology and keyboard users have no named control to operate. Is that acceptable for this story, or should it be raised as an accessibility defect against the application?
ambiguities.impact: AC-ETA-411-006 can only be automated through a non-semantic CSS id selector, which the framework treats as a last-resort locator requiring a VALIDATED waiver. More importantly, whether this is a product defect is a human judgement about the application, not something requirement analysis may decide. If it is a defect, ETA-411 may need to assert an accessible name that does not exist today, in which case the criterion as written would pass while the real problem went unrecorded.
ambiguities.resolution: The reviewer accepts the Command Center control as it is. It is not raised as an accessibility defect against the application, and AC-ETA-411-006 asserts only that activating the control returns the user Home. Automation may address it through the non-semantic id selector #bannerBackground, which requires a 'VALIDATED -' waiver comment under SEM-AUTOMATION-HYGIENE. Recorded consequence: the control still exposes no accessible name, so a keyboard or assistive-technology user has no named control to operate, and this artifact deliberately leaves that unrecorded as a defect on the reviewer's instruction.

ambiguities.question: How should Preferences be reached from the header navigation? AMB-ETA-411-001 brought the header duplicates into scope, but the header exposes no Preferences link. The only header-area route to /ssweb/setup/prefs/preferences.eo is a menu link labelled 'Organization', which is a different name for the same destination as the Preferences dashboard tile. Is the 'Organization' menu link in scope as the third navigation route, is the Preferences dashboard tile the only in-scope route to that page, or is 'Organization' a distinct destination that happens to share a URL?
ambiguities.impact: If the 'Organization' link is in scope, a further criterion is needed and the header-navigation coverage is symmetric across all three destinations. If it is not, AC-ETA-411-007 through AC-ETA-411-009 cover two destinations by two routes and Preferences by one, which is an asymmetry a reviewer should accept knowingly rather than discover in the test plan. The naming difference also matters on its own: a link labelled 'Organization' leading to a page called Preferences may itself be a product inconsistency, but deciding that is a human judgement about the application and not something requirement analysis may settle.
